title: Medea on Stage
subtitle: Corinth, a poisoned robe, and the end no audience forgets

learningObjectives.text: Why is Medea in Corinth, and what goes wrong?
What does her revenge cost everyone?

argo.author: Apollonius Rhodius
argo.locator: Argonautica 3, opening invocation; Book 3, normalized characters 0-476
argo.excerpt: Come now, Erato, stand by my side, and say next how Jason brought back the fleece to Iolcus aided by the love of Medea. For thou sharest the power of Cypris, and by thy love-cares dost charm unwedded maidens; wherefore to thee too is attached a name that tells of love. Thus the heroes, unobserved, were waiting in ambush amid the thick reed-beds; but Hera and Athena took note of them, and, apart from Zeus and the other immortals, entered a chamber and took counsel together
argo.note: Verbatim passage from Seaton's translation of Apollonius' Greek epic; it frames the quest as aided by Medea.

narrativeBlocks.title: Exile in Corinth
narrativeBlocks.body: After Iolcus, Jason and Medea settle in Corinth with their two young sons — the sorceress now a foreign wife in a Greek city, her power reduced to what a marriage gives her.

narrativeBlocks.title: The marriage that erases her
narrativeBlocks.body: Jason announces he will marry Creon's daughter — a royal, legitimate Greek match. Medea's protests mean nothing legally; the stranger who won her everything now treats her as disposable.

narrativeBlocks.title: The gift robe
narrativeBlocks.body: Medea's revenge begins like a reconciliation: she sends the princess a golden robe and crown — gifts steeped in poison that burns the girl and her father alive when she puts them on.

narrativeBlocks.title: The unthinkable cut
narrativeBlocks.body: Then comes the act Euripides makes unbearable: to take from Jason the only thing he has left, Medea kills their two sons herself. Not madness — deliberate, argued, chosen. She escapes to Athens in the dragon-chariot of her grandfather the Sun.

narrativeBlocks.title: Where you've met her
narrativeBlocks.body: That Athens refuge is why Medea is sitting at Aegeus's court when Theseus arrives in week 1 — the poisoned-cup scene is her second act, not her first.

quiz.prompt: Why does Jason's marriage to Creon's daughter provoke Medea?

choices.text: It voids the bargain with Aeetes
It prevents their sons inheriting Argos
It casts her aside — a foreign wife with no legal standing — after she betrayed her family for him
It is arranged by the gods

quiz.explanation: Everything she gave up — father, brother, home — was traded for this marriage, now dissolved at will.

quiz.prompt: What does Medea's revenge consist of?

choices.text: She burns the palace with everyone inside
She sends him back to Colchis in chains
A poisoned robe that kills the princess and Creon — then the killing of her own two sons to destroy Jason completely

quiz.explanation: Euripides makes her vengeance total and her reasoning legible — that is what makes the play horrifying.
